items.summary: حوثی‌های یمن می‌گویند به پالایشگاه رأس تنوره و منطقه مالی ریاض حمله کرده‌اند. عربستان می‌گوید حمله پهپادی حوثی‌ها به پالایشگاه راس تنوره را خنثی کرده است اما تصاویر ماهواره‌ای ستون دود را بر فراز این پایشگاه نشان می‌دهند که وسعتش حدود ۶۰۰ کیلومتر مربع برآورد شده است. در همین حال دونالد ترامپ گفته است که بودجه جنگ با ایران تا پایان ژانویه ۲۰۲۷ تامین شده است.

items.title: کشته شدن دو ایتالیایی در حمله پهپادی به تاسیسات نظامی کویت؛ ایران: نقشی نداشتیم
items.summary: در پی کشته شدن دو ایتالیایی در حمله پهپادی به کویت، ایران هرگونه نقش در این حمله را تکذیب کرد. دولت ایتالیا می‌گوید این دو نفر روی پدافند هوایی کار می کردند و در «حمله پهپادی ایران» به مرکز رادار تاسیسات نظامی کویت کشته شدند. کویت هم این حمله را به ایران نسبت داده است. اما هم سخنگوی ارشد نیروهای مسلح ایران و هم سفارت جمهوری اسلامی در رم، هرگونه نقش تهران در این حمله را رد کرده‌اند. رئیس کمیسیون اروپا در واکنش به این حمله خواستار افزایش فشار بر ایران شد.

items.summary_original: North Korea has temporarily halted shipments of ballistic missiles and artillery shells to Russia following diplomatic friction between the two allies over Moscow's outreach to South Korea, Ukrainian military intelligence said Thursday. According to Ukraine's GUR military intelligence agency, North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui announced the freeze on KN-23 ballistic missile and artillery deliveries last month after Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko suggested Moscow would help de-escalate tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang, Reuters reported. Choe demanded that Russia clarify its policy toward South Korea, GUR said, though Reuters noted it could not independently verify the report or confirm public remarks from either official. PUTIN'S WAR DEATH TOLL REPORTEDLY TOPS 700,000 AS RUSSIA SCRAMBLES FOR RECRUITS The reported pause also suspends Russian military flights over North Korea and stalls a Kremlin request to expand North Korea's troop deployment in Russia from roughly 8,500 to 50,000, according to the outlet. Rudenko, who oversees Asian relations, said last month that Seoul had signaled interest in normalizing ties and resuming direct flights with Moscow once the Ukraine war ends. Despite the reported freeze, North Korean troops remain active in Russia, with 11th Corps units serving in the Kursk region and a missile unit operating in Voronezh since mid-summer, GUR said. items.summary_original: As Americans across the country sit down to Thanksgiving dinner just weeks after Democrats' midterm sweep drastically reshaped the political landscape going into 2027, conversations about politics and the economy could turn tense. Dr. Joel Davis Brown, a leadership expert, executive coach and author who studies how people communicate and navigate conflict, says swapping out the word "but" when discussing controversial topics can help keep the discussions civil. "‘But’ shows disagreement," Brown told Fox News Digital. "It’s a way of telling the person that what they said should not be heard, and it really stifles conversation." Instead, Brown suggests trying "yes, and." That doesn’t mean you have to agree, he said. Rather it signals that you’ve heard the other person and leaves room to share a different view. "‘Yes, I’ve heard you and I have a different opinion,’" Brown said. "We can listen to varying opinions." FOOD PRICES ARE RISING BEFORE THANKSGIVING. AN ECONOMIST SHARES WAYS TO SAVE If a hot-button topic comes up, Brown recommends asking the person to "tell me more about that." The question, he says, can help you understand how someone arrived at their view instead of turning the exchange into a debate. He also cautions against opening with "I disagree," which can put people "in an oppositional place" before they have fully heard one another. items.summary_original: FlyDubai announced Thursday it will resume flights to Tel Aviv, Israel, next week, ending a suspension in place following an attempted hijacking incident in late September, according to media reports. A source familiar with the matter told The Times of Israel that the airline is being allowed back into Israeli airspace "under new security arrangements." The development comes after Transportation Minister Miri Regev decided this week that FlyDubai flights to Israel can resume pending clearance from Shin Bet, Mossad and Israel's National Security Council, the outlet reported. A FlyDubai spokesperson told Reuters that the flights will begin again on Dec. 3. FlyDubai flights to Israel have been suspended since FlyDubai Flight FZ1073 on Sept. 30, when a co-pilot allegedly attacked his captain. FLYDUBAI CO-PILOT ALLEGEDLY PLANNED TO CRASH ISRAEL-BOUND JET AT BEN GURION AIRPORT That plane was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia , where it made a safe landing. "Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian captain of FlyDubai Flight 1073, fought back after being stabbed in the cockpit," according to the Israel Foreign Ministry. items.summary: در انفجار یک پالایشگاه نفت در بانکوک پایتخت تایلند که روز پنجشنبه رخ داد، دست کم 9 نفر مجروح شدند که حال سه نفر وخیم گزارش شده است. این شرکت در بیانیه ای که در فیس بوک منتشر کرد، تایید کرد که انفجار در تاسیسات متعلق به شرکت بانکچاک رخ داده است. این شرکت همچنین مدعی شد که توانسته آتش سوزی بزرگ ناشی از انفجار را ظرف 30 دقیقه پس از انفجار کنترل و خاموش کند. خدمه اضطراری در واکنش به انفجار مهیب در پالایشگاه نفت منطقه نیواورلئان: کلانتر علاوه بر این، مدعی شد نظارت هیچ کاهشی در کیفیت هوای عادی نشان نداد. از زمان وقوع این حادثه، این شرکت به طور مداوم کیفیت هوا را در زمان واقعی با استفاده از ایستگاه‌های نظارت خودکار کیفیت هوای محیط (AQM) که شرکت در Phra Khanong، Bang Na و Bang Nam Phueng نصب کرده است، بررسی کرده است.
items.summary_original: At least nine people have been injured in an oil refinery explosion in Bangkok, Thailand, on Thursday, with three in critical condition. The explosion occurred at a Bangchak Corporation-owned facility, the company confirmed in a statement posted to Facebook. The company also claimed it was able to control and extinguish a large blaze caused by the explosion within 30 minutes of the blast. EMERGENCY CREWS RESPONDING TO MASSIVE EXPLOSION AT NEW ORLEANS-AREA OIL REFINERY: SHERIFF Additionally, it claimed monitoring showed no reduction in normal air quality. "Since the incident occurred, the company has continuously monitored air quality in real time using automatic ambient air quality monitoring (AQM) stations, which the company has installed in the Phra Khanong, Bang Na, and Bang Nam Phueng areas to measure air quality around the refinery resulting from operations," the company wrote. TWO INJURED AFTER EXPLOSION RIPS THROUGH CHEMICAL PLANT, SPARKING HAZMAT RESPONSE, SHELTER-IN-PLACE ORDER "It was found that the air quality in the surrounding area of the refinery is within normal standards. Furthermore, at 5: 30 PM (17: 30 hrs.), the Pollution Control Department measured the air quality within a 3–4 km radius around the refinery—the same radial area—and confirmed that the measurement results are within normal standards," the statement added. The company said it has also paused all production operations at the facility. 'PURE HELL' IN MOSCOW AS UKRAINIAN DRONES STRIKE MAJOR REFIN

items.summary_original: As 2026 comes to a close, several political blunders, missteps, and serious allegations have left prominent politicians and notable figures presumably looking back with regret. Here are the top political turkeys who made headlines for unfortunate reasons this year. Heading into 2026, Eric Swalwell was a well-known member of Congress and the leading Democratic contender in the race for governor of California. By March, he had become the frontrunner in the race and looked poised to take control of the nation’s largest economy in a state where Democrats rarely lose in statewide general elections. Shortly after, that all changed when allegations of sexual assault and other misconduct surfaced in April, prompting prominent Democrats to swiftly withdraw their endorsements and call for Swalwell to abandon his gubernatorial bid. SWALWELL’S FORMER DEM RIVAL UNLOADS ON HIS ‘LIGHTWEIGHT’ CAREER AS SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS EMERGE Swalwell denied the sexual assault allegations, but within days he suspended his campaign and resigned from Congress amid bipartisan calls for his ouster, which effectively ended his political career and put him in potential legal jeopardy. Swalwell faces a federal investigation and separate probes in New York and Los Angeles into sexual assault allegations, which he denies. items.summary_original: Egyptian authorities said Thursday that a driver suspected of causing a fuel tanker crash in Cairo — sparking a massive inferno described by a witness as "God’s hellfire" and leaving 31 dead — has been taken into custody. The deadly blaze erupted Wednesday during rush hour on a major highway surrounding the Egyptian capital, burning 27 vehicles and also leaving 26 injured. As of Thursday, traffic on the Ring Road returned to normal after most of the wreckage was cleared. "It was God’s hellfire on the Ring Road," Salah Ahmed, a microbus driver who witnessed the inferno, told The Associated Press. "People are still in shock." Another witness said to Reuters that victims were found trapped in their vehicles as "they did not have time to get out." STATE DEPARTMENT PRESSES EGYPT TO RESPECT RELIGIOUS FREEDOM AS CHRISTIAN CONVERT FACES POSSIBLE EXECUTION Video footage taken near the scene showed a blaze completely engulfing the highway as people gathered to look at the flames. Egyptian prosecutors said in a statement that authorities had detained the driver of a vehicle suspected of causing the fuel tanker to overturn, which resulted in the fire. They said the driver told investigators he was speeding between lanes when he hit the oil tanker in the rear right. He then lost control of his car and veered far to the right while one of the fuel truck’s tires burst. That caused the fuel tanker to hit the concrete wall of the highway and overturn, leading to the spill of fuel and the fire

items.summary_original: Norwegian airline Norse Atlantic suspended all flights Thursday as its board warned the company may imminently file for bankruptcy if it can't secure short-term financing. "If a short-term financing solution is not secured urgently, it is the Board's intention to file for bankruptcy," the company said in a statement . The airline, which provides long-haul flights between the U.S. and Europe, said it had been discussing with investors a possible takeover that "would include a financing solution." SHIPPING GIANT WARNS STRAIT OF HORMUZ CHAOS IS 'NEW NORMAL' AS TEHRAN SHIFTS 4M BARRELS But, the company added, "There can be no assurance that a viable solution will be found." Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), which contracts jets from Norse through a wet-lease program, shifted all United Kingdom flights to its own Boeing 777 planes, claiming Norse announced the suspension with no notice as PIA passengers were preparing to board. Norse, amid rising fuel costs from the Iran war , began leasing out its Boeing 787 fleet to other airlines as it struggled to make a profit on trans-Atlantic flights. In July, IndiGo, India's largest carrier, announced it would conclude its own wet-lease program with Norse by the end of October. Norse's stock price plummeted and closed down 85%. Most of its value has been wiped out since the start of the year and the stock is now trading at $0.010. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte are calling on Russia to avoid making any moves "that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war" against Ukraine. The declaration came after the pair got together at Trump's Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida on Thanksgiving Eve for what was described as an "outstanding meeting." However, Russia hit Kyiv with ballistic missiles overnight, according to the mayor of the Ukrainian capital. "The meeting was very impactful, with the war between Russia and Ukraine and the conflict in Iran being the primary subjects, as well as all of the record setting achievements that we have made together at the summits in the Hague and at Ankara," Trump and Rutte said in a joint statement. "We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible," the statement added. "Lastly, we talked about the importance of continuing to expand defense spending and investment in our industrial base, both in the United States and across NATO." items.summary_original: In keeping with tradition, President Donald Trump marked his sixth Thanksgiving in the executive office with the White House’s annual Turkey Pardon ceremony on Tuesday. His plans for Thanksgiving Day this year remain unannounced — but previous holidays offer a preview of how the president likes to spend the day honoring those who can't be at home for the uniquely American holiday due to service to the country. Last year, Trump spent Thanksgiving at Mar-a-Lago participating in his favorite pastime — golf. But he also used the time in what is known as the "Winter White House" to call Maj. Gen. Dave Gardner, commander of the 101st Airborne Division and Joint Task Force–Southern Border, by video conference and talk with troops deployed along the southern border. They met with military families and made Thanksgiving crafts with children. In 2020, during the final Thanksgiving of his first term, Trump remained at the White House and made calls to six deployed military units representing every branch of the armed forces, including troops in Kuwait and sailors aboard the USS Winston Churchill in the Red Sea. items.summary_original: Donald Trump carried Mississippi by nearly 23 points in 2024. Two years later, Democrat Scott Colom won the state’s Senate race, ending a Republican hold that had lasted more than four decades. Colom’s victory was part of a string of Democratic breakthroughs during the midterms in places Trump had carried by double digits. Democrats also won Senate races in Kansas and South Carolina, captured the Texas governor’s office and flipped a Republican-held House seat deep in Trump country in Indiana that had not elected a Democrat since 1990. The results stand out for more than the presidential margins as well — Democrats broke Senate streaks that had lasted decades and defeated Republican incumbents in races many expected the GOP to hold, including one where the Democratic challenger spent next to nothing on television advertisements. FOX NEWS VOTER POLL: HOW DEMOCRATS TOOK CONTROL OF THE SENATE Here are five of the year’s most striking upsets: Trump carried the state by nearly 23 points in 2024, and a Democrat had not won a U.S. Senate race in Mississippi since 1982. Several major election forecasters rated the contest Solid Republican for much of the cycle, before shifting it to Likely Republican as the race tightened. Colom, a district attorney, defeated Republican incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., by less than one percentage point, 49.36% to 48.54%, according to Associated Press election results. items.summary_original: The turkey may be a holiday bargain, but rising prices for meat, dairy and fresh foods could make the rest of the Thanksgiving spread cost much more this year. Richard Volpe, a professor of agribusiness at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo, told Fox News Digital that sustained high energy costs in the midst of the Iran war — particularly for diesel — are pushing up grocery prices just as households prepare to host holiday meals. Surging prices of ham and eggnog, in particular, could put a damper on some holiday favorites. "Most of the biggest increases are things like fruits, vegetables and meats," Volpe said. "Fresh and refrigerated foods feel those costs sooner than shelf-stable products." 7 COSTCO THANKSGIVING FOOD DEALS AND STEALS THAT SHOPPERS CAN'T MISS THIS HOLIDAY SEASON Dairy is also especially energy and transportation intensive, putting holiday staples such as butter and eggnog under pressure. Volpe said shoppers willing to switch brands and take advantage of store promotions can keep holiday meals more affordable . "If you are less worried about brand or banner loyalty, and you’re able to follow promotions and look for these sort of aggressive, enticing deals, there are still ways to achieve savings and to keep those Thanksgiving and holiday dinners relatively affordable," Volpe said. items.summary: جی بی پریتزکر، فرماندار ایلینویز، یک دموکرات، پس از اینکه تصمیم گرفت از برنامه اعتبار مالیاتی بورسیه فدرال انصراف دهد، به قرار دادن سیاست های حزبی بر نیازهای آموزشی کودکان متهم شده است، که باعث انتقاد والدین و گروه های حامی آموزش و پرورش شد. پریتزکر روز سه‌شنبه اعلام کرد که ایالتش در این برنامه که سال گذشته توسط رئیس‌جمهور دونالد ترامپ به عنوان بخشی از قانون یک بیگ زیبا امضا شد، شرکت نخواهد کرد. فرماندار این برنامه را به عنوان کوپن مدرسه توصیف کرد، در حالی که گروه های مدافع استدلال می کردند که او این طرح را نادرست توصیف کرده است. پریتزکر در بیانیه‌ای گفت: «در زمانی که آموزش مدارس دولتی بیش از هر زمان دیگری به سرمایه‌گذاری نیاز دارد، ما نباید از مدارس دولتی برای آموزش خصوصی پول خرج کنیم – به‌ویژه که سیاست‌های دولت ترامپ آموزش را تخریب می‌کند».
items.summary_original: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker , a Democrat, is being accused of putting partisan politics over kids' educational needs after he decided to opt out of the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program, prompting criticism from parents and education advocacy groups. Pritzker announced on Tuesday that his state will not opt into the program, which was signed into law by President Donald Trump last year as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The governor described the program as a school voucher, while advocacy groups argued that he mischaracterized the plan. "At a time when public school education needs investments more than ever, we should not siphon money from public schools for private education – especially as the Trump Administration's policies decimate education," Pritzker said in a statement. "We have a responsibility to do right by all of our students. Taxpayer funding should not subsidize donations to private schools that could discriminate based on religion, sexual orientation, or other characteristics." The program allows people to receive federal tax credits for donations up to $1,700 to authorized scholarship-granting organizations (SGOs), which distribute the donated scholarship funds to eligible families to be used on private or public educational expenses, including private school tuition, tutoring services, textbooks and more. A three-judge panel at the Jerusalem District Court suggested that Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara consider dropping the most serious case against Netanyahu, questioned whether a criminal offense occurred in a second case and recommended resolving a third through a plea deal. "Today, the trial fell apart," Netanyahu said in an evening address following the proceedings, according to The Times of Israel . FROM INTELLIGENCE SHARING TO MISSILE DEFENSE, HOW ISRAEL'S PARTNERSHIP PROTECTS AMERICAN SECURITY "Ten years ago, I said, ‘There will be nothing because there was nothing.’ But it took 10 years for this truth to be revealed to everyone," he said. "Citizens of Israel, this trial must end immediately. And what also needs to end immediately is what came out of it — the hatred, the incitement, the division." The court's intervention dealt a major setback to prosecutors more than six years after Netanyahu's trial began and roughly a decade after authorities launched the initial probe into him. Judges had summoned Baharav-Miara to court Wednesday amid concerns over the strength of the prosecution's evidence and whether continuing the cases served the public interest. The 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that an August decision by the late U. S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein, a Clinton appointee who died in October, that denied Trump's second transfer bid was improper. The criminal case centered on Trump's reimbursement of his then-attorney Michael Cohen, who paid adult film actress Stormy Daniels $130,000 shortly before the 2016 election to keep her from publicizing an alleged sexual encounter with Trump a decade earlier. Trump, who denies the encounter, was found guilty in May 2024 of 34 felony counts of falsifying business records. items.summary_original: The Kremlin on Wednesday dismissed a new investigation estimating that at least 700,000 Russian troops have died in President Vladimir Putin's war against Ukraine , as experts warn that mounting military losses are undermining Moscow's ability to sustain its offensive. The findings, published Monday by independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona , are based on leaked Russian government records and statistical analysis. "The only entity that can officially disclose casualty figures is the Russian Defense Ministry," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Wednesday, according to The Moscow Times. PUTIN'S WAR MACHINE TIED TO TROUBLING RECRUITMENT OF YOUNG WOMEN AS NEW DEALS EMERGE Peskov urged reporters to disregard other figures but offered no updated official death toll. The investigation draws on records obtained by the hacking groups Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow after they breached Russia's federal statistics agency, Rosstat. Researchers identified at least 490,000 registered military deaths by late September 2026. However, delays in registering fatalities and soldiers who remain officially listed as missing but are believed to be dead led researchers to estimate that the actual toll had likely reached 700,000 or more by that time. items.summary_original: Attorney General Todd Blanche is mobilizing civil litigators across the Justice Department in an all-hands-on-deck push to fight tens of thousands of legal filings by detained migrants asking federal courts to review whether their imprisonment is lawful. Blanche issued a three-page memo Tuesday calling on attorneys working outside of immigration issues to assist in the lawsuits described by Blanche as "frivolous" and an attempt to "thwart President Trump's promise to the American people to prioritize their safety and security." The pre-Thanksgiving memo comes as the Justice Department has been hit with 97, 000 habeas corpus petition filings since January 2025, including close to 10,000 new petitions filed since October. Typically, the Justice Department faces only a few hundred habeas corpus cases a year. As President Donald Trump has made mass deportations a centerpiece of his second administration, with Department of Homeland Security figures showing nearly 1.2 million illegal immigrants removed to date, the Justice Department has seen a wave of petitions. items.summary_original: Before polling began to show dire warning signs for the GOP ahead of the midterm elections , some in conservative circles felt they had a not-so-secret weapon that would give them an edge over their Democratic rivals — a massive amount of cash. Across the Republican National Committee, Senate Leadership Fund, Congressional Leadership Fund, National Republican Congressional Committee and the National Republican Senatorial Committee, the GOP brought in roughly $1.7 billion in funds to fuel its ill-fated midterm campaigns. The five equivalent Democratic committees, meanwhile, raised well over $300 million less than that total but walked away with massive pickups in even traditionally deep red strongholds like Texas, South Carolina, Kansas and Mississippi. Experts from across the political spectrum explained this result to Fox News Digital by arguing that the impact of money on politics is less than what many in the public may assume and that massive fundraising hauls can only take a party so far when it faces political headwinds as strong as those weathered by the GOP in the run-up to election night. Vance reportedly worked with Nvidia's board over the weekend to get Huang his job back, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who reportedly warned Trump about intelligence concerning the relationship, took another approach. Rubio has not publicly weighed in on the CEO's reinstatement and his office did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. The Vice President told CNN on Wednesday that Attorney General Todd Blanche assured him that Huang was not under investigation. items.summary_original: Minnesota’s new paid leave law, championed and signed by outgoing Democratic Gov. Tim Walz , is already causing major headaches as public employees take advantage of the program at levels that are straining government services. Eleven months after the law took effect — allowing Minnesota workers up to 12 weeks a year off with partial pay to care for a newborn or a sick family member, and up to 12 weeks to recover from their own serious illness — almost one in four Minneapolis city employees has used the benefit, the Minnesota Star Tribune reported. The outlet reported that the absences are putting a "squeeze" on some departments, including the agency that takes emergency calls in the city. On Tuesday, a clip posted by Alpha News from an October budget presentation to the Minneapolis City Council went viral on social media. In the video, Emergency Communications Center Assistant Director Leticia Cardenas tells the council that 41% of her 911 staff were out on Minnesota’s new Paid Family and Medical Leave program. NEW AUDIT IN WALZ'S BACKYARD EXPOSES MASSIVE FRAUD RISK TIED TO POST-GEORGE FLOYD ACTIVISM The high rate of leave has forced remaining operators to work significant overtime to keep the center staffed around the clock, contributing to a proposed $1.5 million budget increase for the department. Calling the Ukrainian attack "sinful aggression," the LNA also quoted the Quran, writing, "And those who have wronged are going to know to what [kind of] return they will be returned." items.summary_original: Attacks targeting Christians across Europe rose 44% last year, according to a new report from the Vienna-based Observatory on Intolerance and Discrimination Against Christians in Europe (OIDAC). Their research documented 2,465 anti-Christian hate crimes and incidents in 2025, with France , England and Wales, Germany and Austria recording the highest totals. "Our primary concern with the new data is that anti-Christian attacks that target persons, individuals themselves, have risen," OIDAC executive director Anja Tang told Fox News Digital. "Clergy and people responsible for places of worship were those who were most attacked and also where numbers increased most strongly." CHRISTIAN WOMAN PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO NEW 'ORWELLIAN' CHARGES FOR STANDING AND SILENT PRAYER She added, "These would be people who were present, were visible, recognizable as Christians and kind of associated with a church." Tang noted that while OIDAC’s numbers are "quite conservative," saying "aggression against individuals is highly underreported" across Europe. The group said French authorities recorded a 70% increase in attacks on individuals, the highest in Europe, although Tang notes the French government has not yet published a detailed explanation of the increase. OIDAC argues the increase in attacks against individuals warrants separate attention from incidents involving vandalism, theft and arson targeting religious property. items.summary_original: A federal grand jury in Minnesota is hearing evidence in the investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., sources told Fox News. Federal prosecutors described the case in newly unsealed court records as a "pre-indictment investigation." It remains unclear what evidence the panel has heard or whether it will return charges. There are at least two active investigations underway, according to sources: One into allegations of immigration fraud and another into Omar's finances. ILHAN OMAR APPEARS CLUELESS ON BASIS FOR FEDERAL PROBES: ‘YOU PROBABLY HAVE MORE DETAILS ON THAT’ Omar has repeatedly denied wrongdoing to Fox News Digital in connection with the investigations, but the investigations remain ongoing, and no official charges have been filed to date. The immigration investigation reportedly originated under then-President Barack Obama, while former President Joe Biden's administration opened the investigation into her finances. In a detail sources say is relevant to the immigration probe, court records use three versions of Omar’s name. Investigators are examining whether she used a false name or birthdate to obtain U.S. citizenship. items.summary_original: Criticism is mounting among experts concerned with the U.S. Army's "risky" plan to resume helicopter training flights near Washington National Airport following a deadly midair collision in 2025. The Army released a plan and told select members of Congress it wants to restart helicopter test flights near DCA — just a few miles from the Pentagon — as soon as Dec. 1, 2026. Backlash immediately ensued. Rep. Don Beyer, D-Va., asserted on X he has "grave concerns about the decision to resume training flights before the NTSB’s safety recommendations have been fully implemented." A spokesperson for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) told Fox News Digital that it "has not received a formal request to resume military helicopter flights around Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA)." "Approval from the agency is required before any training in the area can restart," the spokesperson added. FAA, NTSB INVESTIGATING POSSIBLE VIOLATION OF SAFETY PROTOCOL INVOLVING TRUMP, MARINE ONE A U.S. Army Black Hawk helicopter collided with American Airlines Flight 5342 in January 2025, killing all 67 people aboard both aircrafts. The FAA subsequently halted military helicopter training flights in the area in May 2025 after another Black Hawk helicopter flew too close to DCA, forcing air traffic controllers to reroute some commercial flights. Through her film, "The Lost Jews of the Inquisition," Laurie Cardoza-Moore told Fox News Digital that she hopes to help people like herself uncover a history they may not even know their families carry. She says the Israeli government believes there could be millions of "Anussim," or hidden Jews. "Some know their family history, while others don’t," she said. She is also a member of the Tennessee Textbook and Instructional Materials Quality Commission. For Cardoza-Moore, the journey began in 2002, in the aftermath of 9/11, when she decided to introduce a resolution in the Tennessee state legislature expressing support for Israel in its war on terror. The following year, she was invited by the Jewish Federation of Nashville on a mission to Israel. items.summary_original: The Trump administration’s efforts to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia have set a new bar for shaping a private corporation, according to Eric Schiffer, chairman and CEO of Reputation Management Consultants, a crisis management and brand protection firm. "Trump came in to really give a second life to Jensen, where he would have been dead," Schiffer told Fox News Digital Tuesday. Schiffer said the intervention has opened a kind of Pandora’s box that Democrats may seek to exploit to benefit ideological allies in the private sector. Still, he said the national security interests underpinning Trump’s efforts to intervene on behalf of Huang fall within the responsibilities of the presidency. JENSEN HUANG'S NVIDIA RETURN SENDS CHINA A CLEAR MESSAGE: THE AI RACE IS ON Asked whether he believes Democrats may use the moment as a precedent to tip the scales in favor of ideological allies down the road, Schiffer said he sees that possibility in the cards. "I think that, of course, they would have that capability. I think that that is a risk," Schiffer said. But Schiffer said the justification would likely depend on the circumstances. "If the Democrats had a similar situation or it's a leading organization that is so critical to both national security and the economy, then it would make sense," Schiffer said. The controversy comes as the Cincinnati-based grocer begins executing a three-year plan it has previously announced to cut $5 billion in costs as part of a restructuring that will eliminate roughly 37% of its U.S. corporate workforce by 2029. While Kroger maintains the reductions are aimed at lowering shelf prices through technology and leaner operations, simultaneous recruiting for a new hub in Bangalore has fueled online accusations that the company is offshoring American jobs while asking shoppers to bear high food prices. items.summary_original: Congress is nearing the deadline to avert a government shutdown, and Senate Republicans are taking a leap of faith as the clock ticks: trusting Senate Democrats to dodge a holiday disaster. When the upper chamber returns on Nov. 30, there will be just shy of two weeks for both sides to reach an agreement to thwart another partisan closure. At the center of the issue is the Iran war: Democrats intend to use the government’s purse strings to bring the eight-month conflict to an end. Republicans, meanwhile, want to put together an emergency supplemental funding package with hundreds of billions of dollars dedicated to the military, munitions and war effort. items.summary_original: Excerpts from the late Pope Francis ' private diary published Tuesday reveal that the pontiff endured a two-year spiritual crisis beginning in 2021, writing that he felt tempted by the devil and struggled with the weight of wielding power over the Catholic Church. The 160-page volume, "The Private Diary of Pope Francis," was compiled by Cardinal Victor Fernandez and spans entries from December 1992 through August 2024 — eight months before Francis died in April 2025 at age 88 — marking the first papal diary made public since the 1960s. In a December 2022 entry, Francis described his crisis as "all mixed with governance issues, pressure regarding decisions to make, and aridity and desolation," adding that he resisted becoming a leader "who uses others like puppets." MYSTERIOUS BLOOD-SOAKED RELIC LINKED TO HISTORY'S MOST BELOVED SAINT, ST. FRANCIS OF ASSISI, GOES ON DISPLAY Across the entries, Francis wrote that he believed he had seen the devil three times — including during a Vatican meeting — and recalled a June 2018 vision of hell . "Last night I saw the entrance to Hell," he wrote in the 2018 entry. "I peeked in to look a little, and it terrified me. I grabbed the Rosary as a weapon. I thank the Lord for this help." Reacting Tuesday on "Varney Co.," Fox News contributor and theologian Jonathan Morris said he was most struck not by the late pope's spiritual struggles , but by the Vatican's decision to publish them. items.summary_original: Israel accused Iran of developing chemical weapons Tuesday and raised the possibility of a preemptive strike to prevent Tehran from using them, warning that the regime seeks a strategic advantage after major setbacks in its war with Israel and the United States. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz told reporters in Tel Aviv that Israel and the U.S. have intelligence indicating Iran began developing chemical weapons after their joint military campaign launched Feb. 28. Katz declined to disclose how far the program has progressed or where the weapons are being developed, though he noted Israeli intelligence has monitored Iran's effort for months and said that operational plans are in place. BLINKEN WARNS US GROUND INVASION OF IRAN WOULD BE 'ABSOLUTE DISASTER' AS TEHRAN ESCALATES ATTACKS "Iran is in the process of developing chemical weapons," Katz said, according to Israel's i24NEWS . "This intelligence information reached both the United States and Israel," he said. "Israel is determined not to allow Iran to acquire this kind of chemical weapons capability that would threaten the country and the entire region," he added. Katz described the program as a potentially game-changing threat to Israel and the broader Middle East, warning that the weapons could give Tehran leverage to rebuild its depleted military infrastructure, including its nuclear program . items.summary_original: Poland announced Tuesday it had renewed its push for a permanent U.S. military presence in the country after two Russian airspace incursions in four days, including one in which a Swedish fighter jet under NATO command was cleared to shoot down a Russian cruise missile but held its fire. The latest incursion came overnight Nov. 24, when a Russian drone briefly entered Polish airspace during attacks on Ukraine, four days after three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles had crossed into Poland, prompting NATO to scramble fighter jets and bolster air defenses along its eastern flank. Poland's chargé d'affaires in Washington, Bogdan Klich, said Tuesday that he briefed the White House National Security Council on the violations and renewed Warsaw's call to permanently station American troops in the NATO member country. US URGES AMERICANS IN HISTORIC REGION TO STAY ALERT AFTER 'DANGEROUS' AIRSPACE INCIDENT "Yesterday, I briefed the U.S. National Security Council on the violation of Polish airspace by Russian Kh-101 missiles and once again discussed the issue of the permanent deployment of U.S. troops in Poland," Klich wrote on X . The new diplomatic push follows the incidents involving Russian assets and heightened concerns that Moscow's war in Ukraine will spill into NATO territory . The Nov. 20 incursion involved a Swedish JAS 39 Gripen pilot operating under NATO command who was authorized to engage a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile, according to Lt. Gen. items.summary_original: Russia is growing increasingly willing to take risks against NATO countries, with a mounting campaign of sabotage, arson attacks and assassination plots that could escalate within weeks or months, Latvia’s president warned in an interview with Fox News Digital. Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs said Western leaders may be underestimating the threat posed by Russian President Vladimir Putin because they fail to fully understand the ideological and historical beliefs driving the Kremlin’s foreign policy. "The appetite for the risk is growing in Russia," Rinkēvičs said. "We see numbers of arson attacks. Some assassination plots. Acts of sabotage." BATTLE-TESTED ZELENSKYY SOUNDS CHILLING ALARM ON WHERE PUTIN’S WAR COULD HEAD NEXT While Russian provocations have so far remained below the threshold that would trigger NATO’s collective defense mechanism under Article 5, Rinkēvičs warned that the situation could deteriorate rapidly. "We see that the number of attacks is rising, but we still see that, at this point, it may change very quickly. It may change maybe in weeks or months or a couple of months' time," he said. The Latvian leader pointed to recent cooperation between Latvian and Estonian intelligence services that he said resulted in arrests in Estonia and prevented an attack against a defense factory. items.summary_original: Ukraine's former prosecutor general is accusing President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's administration of interfering in a criminal investigation involving the head of the country's anti-corruption bureau after the president demanded his removal from office in September. In an extensive interview with Fox News Digital, Ruslan Kravchenko alleged that Zelenskyy's decision to remove him came under pressure from the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU) and the Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAPO), whose officials he said his office had been investigating. "The signature on the resignation letter was mine. The decision was his," Kravchenko said. "You do not have to put handcuffs on the president himself to tie his hands. It is enough to put the people he relies on at risk." He claims the president's office instructed prosecutors to close a criminal case involving NABU Director Semen Kryvonos. "The Office of the President began issuing instructions to the Office of the Prosecutor General to immediately close the criminal case against the head of NABU," he said. "In my assessment, that amounts to deliberate interference in an investigation." items.summary_original: As antisemitism surges across the United States and around the world in the wake of Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, massacre, policy strategist and public speaker Gabe Groisman is urging American Jews to stand their ground and fight for the future of their community — and the soul of the nation. In his new book, "The Jewish Fight for America," Groisman, a former mayor of Bal Harbour, Florida, explores the history of American Jews and their contributions to the country, arguing that despite rising antisemitism, they should confront the tide of hate and stand firm in their rightful place. "The first fight we have to take on here in the U.S. is to strengthen the community, to try to teach our brothers and sisters about who we are as a people," Groisman told Fox News Digital. "Then we can get to the part of why the Land of Israel is important to us, why Jewish sovereignty over the Land of Israel, which is the State of Israel today, is an integral part of who we are as Jews in America or anywhere in the world." Speaking at the 72nd annual session of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin , Rutte cautioned that competing military command structures could hold up decisions in a crisis, warning that Russia’s "war machine" is running at full throttle and could also pose a threat to Europe long after the war ends. "What I would counsel against is having all the nations with their own militaries working together in NATO and then on top of that having a big European structure, because then if Putin attacks, we will first need two or three weeks to agree who will do what, and then he will probably end up in Rotterdam before we have decided. So that has been my argument," Rutte said, according to Ukrainska Pravda . items.summary_original: Russia warned Monday that it could carry out a "preventive nuclear attack" under certain circumstances, with former President Dmitry Medvedev claiming Ukraine and NATO allies have already crossed certain thresholds that could push Moscow to consider using nuclear weapons. "The massive use of non-nuclear means that cause catastrophes makes a preventive nuclear attack by the Russian Federation possible," Medvedev, deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council , wrote in an article published Monday in the Moscow Journal of International Law and excerpted by the state news agency TASS . Medvedev also warned that "secret or hidden supplies of nuclear weapons from the West to Kyiv will provoke a legitimate preventive nuclear attack by Russia." MOSCOW THREATENS NUCLEAR RESPONSE OVER TINY FORTRESS WEDGED BETWEEN US ALLIES AS CLASH FEARS GROW "Kyiv and its allies must remember that the Russian Federation not only has the right, but in various situations has the obligation to use nuclear weapons," he wrote. Medvedev's warning came amid continuing tensions between Moscow and the West over the nearly five-year war in Ukraine and NATO's military support for Kyiv. He argued that Ukraine and its Western allies have already created circumstances under which Russia could consider a nuclear strike, though he said Russian President Vladimir Putin carefully weighs the consequences before making such a decision. items.summary_original: Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit within less than 60 days according to new Western intelligence assessments reported Monday, raising fears that Moscow is preparing to deploy a weapon capable of crippling thousands of satellites used by the United States and its allies. The intelligence reports emerged just four days after President Donald Trump met with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping at a high-profile summit in Shenzhen, China, where nuclear arms control was a central topic. The three leaders issued a joint declaration affirming that nuclear war should never be fought, but stopped short of announcing binding arms-control commitments. According to a joint investigation published Nov. 23 by German broadcasters WDR and NDR and the newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung, Western intelligence agencies believe Russia has assembled a satellite known as "Sputnik-S," which has reportedly been stored in the Moscow region for several years. Intelligence warnings shared among several NATO countries in early November indicated that the satellite, reportedly designed to carry a nuclear warhead, could be launched within 60 days. items.summary_original: After nine years in a Rome prison , the captain of the Costa Concordia, Francesco Schettino, was released early from prison. Italian newspaper Quotidiano Nazionale reports he will serve the remaining 7 years of his 16-year sentence for manslaughter on supervised probation. Schettino’s lawyer, Francesca Carnicelli, told Fox News, "I can confirm that Mr. Schettino is currently finishing his sentence under a program that allows him to live outside of prison," saying, "he has a job as an office worker, must be home by 10:00 p.m. and is not allowed to leave the province where he resides." CRUISE COMPANY FOUNDER SAYS HE'S 'THE VILLAIN' AFTER 200-PLUS PASSENGERS ARE STRANDED Almost 15 years ago, on Jan. 13, 2012, the Costa Concordia slammed into rocks off Tuscany’s Giglio island. Schettino reportedly veered off course to perform a "sail-by salute." There were 4,200 passengers and crew on board, and 32 people were killed. Schettino faced backlash after abandoning the ship , while hundreds of passengers were waiting to be rescued. At the time, Schettino told Italian La Repubblica that while helping others he tripped and ended up in one of the lifeboats.
